key_insight: The paper shows that conventional FPV can decouple flamelet state from the local strain field, while an $\varepsilon$-based coupling keeps non-premixed flamelet behavior consistent with the modeled turbulence.
engineering_relevance: Using $\varepsilon$ to set flamelet strain improves physical consistency in RANS combustion models for transonic reacting shear layers, especially near quenching and high-strain regions.
method: 2D RANS simulations of a transonic accelerating reacting mixing layer
Compare one-step chemistry, conventional FPV, and the proposed $\varepsilon$-$Z$ flamelet model
Use $\varepsilon$ to infer flamelet strain rate $S^*$ and transport selected species explicitly
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the models were evaluated by comparing the RANS mean strain-rate field with the strain rate imposed on the flamelet, showing FPV preferentially samples near-equilibrium states in high-strain regions.
watch_item: The approach still depends on modeled turbulence and tabulated flamelet assumptions, so accuracy may be sensitive to how $\varepsilon$, flammability limits, and reactant-availability scaling are implemented.
